clue.text: Indicator illuminated, has to set off

parts.note: lit means lit up, illuminated

indicators.note: 'off' can mean departing from the usual state, so the letters are thrown out of their normal order

parts.note: 'has to' and 'must' both express obligation
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone switches on a warning light, which then has to set off an alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last word's letters are shuffled; the first two pieces are plain synonyms run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive trial that reveals the true nature of something serves as an indicator, just as the paper strip shows acid or alkali.

indicators.note: taking the lid off a word removes its top, which in a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: a glass is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: Someone removes the cover from a container meant for a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: GLASS loses its G, the top letter in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a young woman, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Grovelling lot offering foreign aid in lower digits

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: toes are the digits on the lower limbs, as fingers are on the upper

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A servile group offers overseas assistance, maybe while bowing low at someone's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower digits' are toes rather than fingers; 'offering' is a joining word, and 'in' puts the shuffled letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies are sycophants who fawn on the powerful, so as a group they are a grovelling crowd.

clue.text: Knickers etc the scoundrel waved about

indicators.note: something waved about is tossed every which way, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: twelve letters taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A rogue brandishes a pair of knickers, perhaps stolen from a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'etc' widens the definition from one garment to the whole class it belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are an example of the garments worn beneath outer clothing, and 'etc' extends it to all such items.

clue.text: Woman of iron, man of straw?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Margaret, the British prime minister nicknamed the Iron Lady
second meaning: a craftsman who roofs houses with straw or reed

explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher, UK prime minister 1979-90, was dubbed the Iron Lady; 'man of straw' usually means a weak figure, but here it is a roofer working in straw.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the former premier is also the trade name for someone who covers roofs with dried straw or reeds.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put an end to
second meaning: whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as drink ruining someone; the verb sense of putting a stop to something is the less familiar one.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to thwart it, and the same word names the whisky made north of the border.

indicators.note: something penned in is enclosed, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer comes up with a striking headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headline' looks like a noun about newspapers, but it is the verb: to headline a show is to star in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who headlines a show takes the leading role, which is exactly what it means to star.

clue.text: I appreciate that strong cheese, crisp and silky stuff

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
F stands for forte, Italian for strong or loud in music
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a host for a pungent cheese and some crisps, then mentions something silky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong cheese' wants to be one item, but 'strong' gives its own letter and the cheese follows. 'Crisp' belongs to the definition, describing the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a stiff, lustrous woven fabric, often of silk, so crisp and silky material describes it well.

parts.note: Roy and Al, two short male names
to flush is to cleanse with a rush of water

explanation.surface: An instruction to help bath two young lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' looks like a verb meaning give, but it is a poker hand; 'little boys' means short boys' names.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the top-ranking combination is ace to ten in one suit, a hand of cards that beats all others.

parts.note: to snap is to break suddenly
to drag is to pull along
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener snaps and tugs at a weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is the joining word between the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden flower whose blooms open like a mouth when squeezed.

clue.text: Dodgy two shakes, first one ignored

indicators.note: ignoring the opening letter means dropping it from the front of the word

parts.note: 'in two shakes' and 'in a jiffy' both mean very quickly

explanation.surface: Something is suspicious about two shakes, the first of which nobody noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'two shakes (of a lamb's tail)' means a moment, as does a jiffy; its J goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something iffy is doubtful or of questionable quality, the same as something described as dodgy.

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a record playing on so late would keep people awake, read as three words

explanation.surface: A melancholy song played loud keeps the neighbours up at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' looks like a container signal, but the question mark flags a whimsical reading: a disc left on so late.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate means unable to be comforted, a deeper form of sadness or dejection.

indicators.note: coming before something means placed ahead of it in the line

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricketer needs just one run to bring the scores level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw level' reads as one phrase about equalising, but 'level' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows or layers placed one above another, so it is a level.

indicators.note: something coloured has been altered from its original state, so the letters are changed round

parts.note: nine letters taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A milliner dyes a bell-shaped hat a new shade.
explanation.walkthrough: A cloche is a close-fitting bell-shaped hat; 'coloured' fits the dye surface while signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson colouring made from crushed scale insects, used for food and fabric.

clue.text: Two animals, one held by player?

parts.note: first animal: a chirping insect
second animal: a flying mammal

explanation.surface: A pet owner or zookeeper looks after two creatures, one of them cradled by a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests music or games, but it is a batsman, and the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman in the sport grips a willow blade to strike the ball, so it is an implement such a player holds.

indicators.note: something in another thing is enclosed by it

parts.note: ruby is a shade of red
to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: A jeweller repairs a fissure in a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' reads as a noun meaning a flaw, but it is the verb, as in cracking a code.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem that has been resolved has been sorted out, just as one that is fixed.

clue.text: Ultimately careless stroke — that's hard to read

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A sloppy flourish of the pen leaves writing illegible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' looks like a pen stroke, but it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is untidy, careless handwriting, which by its nature is difficult to decipher.

indicators.note: something in another thing is enclosed by it

parts.note: MIN is the abbreviation for minute, a unit of time
a stake is a wooden post driven into the ground

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a letter was mailed on schedule and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' means mail on the surface, but here it is a fence post.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is mistaken holds an incorrect belief, so they are in the wrong.

clue.text: US author recalled in the top academic

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters are read backwards
the letters sit in the following words rather than being built from meanings

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A distinguished American writer is remembered in the company of the finest scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: Truman Capote wrote Breakfast at Tiffany's and In Cold Blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman Capote was an American novelist and journalist, so his surname fits an author from the United States.

parts.note: a plum job or role is the best one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The ideal moment to dress up in one's best clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum as an adjective means choice or most desirable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's feathers are its showy display, and plumage is used figuratively for fine elaborate dress.

parts.note: a tin is a can
nit, short for nitwit, is a fool
US abbreviates United States, hence American

explanation.surface: An agony aunt's reader asks whether a problem can deceive an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb, but it is a tin; 'Listener's problem' suggests a radio audience but means trouble with the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnitus is a ringing or buzzing in the ears, a hearing complaint that afflicts anyone trying to hear.

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letters count

parts.note: the leading letters of the two words
eggs that addle go rotten

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a crazy idea as utter rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' looks like part of the nonsense theme, but it is the verb: an addled egg has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is trivial or foolish talk, a common British word for rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Pub surrounds bordering on Zambia and a market

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it on all sides

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tavern near the Zambian border stands beside a marketplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordering on' reads as geography, but it picks out the edges of the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a market, especially an oriental one, or a sale of goods for charity.

clue.text: Spirited former lover, very industrious creature

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
über is German for over, used in English to mean very or super
the ant is proverbially hard-working

explanation.surface: A lively ex-partner turns out to be an extremely hard worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Uber as an informal prefix means super or ultra, as in uber-cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of energy, excitement and cheerfulness, the same as lively or spirited.

parts.note: the letter O is ring-shaped
an intimate is a close friend, a pal

explanation.surface: A gemstone ring given as a personal, intimate gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun for a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The opal is a gemstone known for its shifting iridescent play of colours.

clue.text: Test of right and left, originally

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only each word's opening letter counts

parts.note: the leading letters of the four words

explanation.surface: An eye or reflex examination checking right and left sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language exam, so it is a kind of test.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put up with
second meaning: a large furry mammal

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures putting up with a shaggy creature; the two meanings are unrelated.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to endure or stand something, and the noun names the shaggy-coated mammal such as a grizzly.

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a backer supports a venture, as a patron does
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An employee serves sugar substitute to a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' suggests sugar, but it is slang for a bribe; a backhander is a British word for a secret payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is informal for an inducement or bribe, and a backhander is a covert payment of the same kind.

indicators.note: abbreviated means cut short, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a tweet is a short message posted on social media

explanation.surface: A sweet note is kept short.
explanation.walkthrough: Twee is usually disparaging, meaning excessively cute, so 'charming' is a generous definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee describes something quaint and dainty, sweetly pretty to the point of excess, a cloying kind of charm.

clue.text: Fruit's outside, awfully large one: half of pear inside

indicators.note: something inside is enclosed by the surrounding letters
awfully suggests badly done, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is just two of its letters

parts.note: the first half of the word, its opening two letters

explanation.surface: Someone describes the skin of a huge fruit with part of a pear stuck in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit's outside' is the definition, not a container instruction; the possessive belongs to the fruit whose rind is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel is the rind or skin of citrus fruit, so the outer layer of one such fruit is its peel.
